tests.name: Quick Check
tests.description: Timed check on The Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram

questions.question: Q: What are the axes of the HR diagram?
questions.correctAnswer: Vertical axis: luminosity or absolute magnitude (increasing upward). Horizontal axis: temperature or spectral class (decreasing left to right — hot stars on the left).

questions.question: Q: Where are white dwarfs found on the HR diagram and why?
questions.correctAnswer: Lower-left: they are hot (high temperature) but dim (low luminosity) because they are very small.

questions.question: Q: Why are red giants luminous despite being cool?
questions.correctAnswer: Because they have enormous surface area — luminosity depends on both temperature and radius (L ∝ R²T⁴), so a very large radius compensates for low temperature.

tests.name: Exam-Style Practice
tests.description: Short-answer practice on The Hertzsprung-Russell Diagram

questions.question: Q: What is the period-luminosity relationship of Cepheid variables?
questions.correctAnswer: Longer pulsation periods correspond to higher luminosities. This allows Cepheids to be used as standard candles for distance measurement.

questions.question: Q: Where is the Sun located on the HR diagram?
questions.correctAnswer: On the main sequence, roughly in the middle — it is a G2V star with moderate luminosity and temperature.
